title: Reading journal: LLM efficiency & evaluation sketches
content:
Quick context / purpose:
- Personal reading log for ideas that might become infra experiments or evals for RW inference. Informal, scratchy. Not a formal PRD.
- Focus: concrete techniques to reduce per-token cost and lower p50/p95 latency without degrading output quality on real product prompts.

Notes from papers & talks (high level):
1) 'Adaptive prefix caching for long-lived chat sessions' (notes on a talk, not exact title)
   - Idea: track common prompt prefixes across customers, maintain per-tenant small prefix cache on GPU/host for hot prompts.
   - Tradeoffs: TTL eviction vs LRU; privacy if prefixes contain PII. For private deployments we can pin prefixes at customer config level.
   - Implementation thought: use small LRU keyed by (customer, route, prompt-hash) in shared memory, warm KV cache pointer to GPU when frequently accessed.

2) Quantization + selective fp16 for K/V layers (paper: quant-aware layer fusion)
   - Key takeaway: quantize feed-forward and attention matmul weights to 4-bit, keep softmax/LayerNorm in higher precision to preserve stability.
   - Performance: reported 1.8-2.6x throughput improvement dependent on sequence length and batching scheme.
   - Risk: distribution shift on rare tokens -> do small QA evals on prompt sets before rollout.

3) Micro-batching vs continuous batching (notes from infra meetup)
   - Continuous (streaming) batching gives lower p50 for low QPS and better GPU utilization for mixed-size requests.
   - Micro-batches tuned to seq-length buckets can reduce stray padding token work. Need per-model bucket histograms.
   - Experimental metric: measure tokens-per-second normalized by utilized flops (approx) and p99 latency.

4) Eval methods for hallucination / factuality drift (paper + slide notes)
   - Use small targeted prompt sets derived from customer logs (anonymized) to catch regressions after quantization or model swap.
   - Automate differential testing: sample N prompts per release, compute hallucination score + BLEU-style overlap vs reference answers.

Immediate takeaways / heuristics to try on Redwood stack:
- Prefix caching: run small A/B on dev cluster using a per-customer in-memory cache of top-100 prompt prefixes; route warm hits to a pinned worker with pre-initialized kv cache. Measure p50 and p95 on chat workloads.
- Quantization can be rolled gradually: shadow-infer with quantized kernels on limited traffic path and compare logits divergence and quality metrics. Must tie to eval suite.
- Batching: implement histogram-based per-model micro-batch sizes (3 buckets: short/medium/long) and a fallback continuous-batching mode. Compare cost/TPS.

Sketch of an experiment (minimal repro):
- Cluster: dev-dedicated-0 (2x A100 equivalent)
- Model: open-llm/gpt-small-7b-q4 (simulated quant)
- Workload: 1k recorded user prompts (anonymized) split by length; inject 10% long-context prompts to observe pad overhead.
- Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, token-cost estimate (dollars/token), quality delta via evaluation prompts (10 QA items).
- Duration: run 3 hours per configuration to capture variability.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to pick prefix TTL adaptively? Heuristic: decay when last-used > 24h, but customer patterns may be diurnal. Maybe use exponential decay on hit rate.
- Edge-case: mixed multi-tenant host GPU — isolation and noisy-neighbor effects when pinning. Need a capacity policy to limit pinned workers per-customer.
- Quantized model compatibility across kernel libs (Flash/Trt/oneDNN) — runtime needs capability detection and fallback strategy.

Actionable todos (for me / IC sprint):
- [ ] Put together a small eval harness (pytest style) that can run shadow quantized inference and compute mean logit difference + 3 quality metrics. (linked to INF-1289)
- [ ] Prototype in-memory prefix cache in the local serving stub; simple LRU with TTL and per-tenant namespace. Record hit/miss rates.
- [ ] Collect 2k anonymized chat prefixes from product logs (coordinate with product/CS for opt-out list).
- [ ] Run micro-batch bucket profiler on recent production model traces to pick bucket boundaries.

Loose notes / ideas to revisit later:
- Consider 'cheap verifier' rerank step: cheap small model (2B quantized) verifies outputs on expensive model and suppresses hallucinations. Could be a wider rollout pattern instead of full model rollback.
- Cost-aware routing: if a customer is on Dedicated but hitting SLOs often, try routing burst traffic to a cheaper quantized variant with automatic rollback if quality metric fails.
- Could instrument per-token energy/compute estimator into the console so product folks see unit economics per route.

References I flagged while reading:
- arXiv:2403.01234 (adaptive caching)
- internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/412 (micro-batching scheduler prototype)
- INF-1289 (Confluence/Jira: quantized-shadow rollouts)
- Slack thread: infra-general thread on quantization tradeoffs (linked above)

Random thoughts / scratch (TBD):
- If prefix cache hit rate > 20% for a route and avg prefix length > 40 tokens, we probably save enough KV reads to justify pinning. Need math: saved KV iterations * avg tokens * cost_per_token -> dollars saved per hour.
- For private deployments: expose a knob to pin/unpin prefixes in customer's control plane UI (small UX effort).

Last quick log: 2026-04-15 09:10 — chatted with Aisha about experiment plan; she suggested running warmup-phase with synthetic prompts to validate cache correctness before using real logs.

-- end of scratch log --
